highlights:
Authentication

The Gemini Notebook API uses OAuth 2.0 to authenticate requests on behalf of a Google user. Every request must include an OAuth 2.0 Bearer token in the `Authorization` HTTP header. The API doesn't accept API keys.

## Before you begin Copy link to this section: Before you begin

- Create or select a Google Cloud project. You enable the API, configure the OAuth consent screen, and create OAuth clients in this project. To create a project, see Create a Google Cloud project.
- Use a personal Google Account. During the Public Preview, the Gemini Notebook API is only available for personal Google Accounts. Requests authenticated with a Google Workspace account fail with `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` (`WORKSPACE_ACCOUNT_NOT_SUPPORTED`).
- Sign in to Gemini Notebook once. The API reads and writes the notebooks of the authorizing user, so each Google Account must have signed in to Gemini Notebook at least once before calling the API. If an account has never signed in to Gemini Notebook, `CreateNotebook` requests fail with `404 NOT_FOUND` (`Account not found for user.`).

Copy link to this section: OAuth 2.0 scopes

Requests must be authenticated with an OAuth 2.0 token granted one of the following scopes:

| Scope | Access | Supported methods |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/notebook` | Read and write access to notebooks and sources | `CreateNotebook`, `GetNotebook`, `ListNotebooks`, `UpdateNotebook`, `CreateSource`, `GetSource`, `ListSources` |
| `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/notebook.readonly` | Read-only access to notebooks and sources | `GetNotebook`, `ListNotebooks`, `GetSource`, `ListSources` |

0 for your application

To integrate the Gemini Notebook API into a web, desktop, or production application, follow the steps in Using OAuth 2.0 to Access Google APIs to create an OAuth 2.0 client ID in your Google Cloud project:

1. Enable the API: In the Google Cloud Console, select your Google Cloud project and enable the Gemini Notebook API (`notebook.googleapis.com`).
2. Configure the OAuth consent screen: Go to the Google Auth Platform branding page to configure your app details, and add the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/notebook` scope on the Data Access page.
3. Create an OAuth 2.0 client ID: Go to the Clients page, click Create client, and select your application type (for example, Desktop app or Web application). Download the client configuration JSON file as `client_secret.json`.
4. Request an access token and call the API: Follow the OAuth 2.0 flow for your application type to obtain an access token and pass it in the `Authorization: Bearer` header:

```
from google_auth_oauthlib.flow import InstalledAppFlow
import requests

SCOPES = ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/notebook"]

flow = InstalledAppFlow.from_client_secrets_file("client_secret.json", SCOPES)
creds = flow.run_local_server(port=0)

resp = requests.get(
    "https://notebook.googleapis.com/v1/notebooks",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {creds.token}"},
)
print(resp.json())

```

```
curl -s -X GET "https://notebook.googleapis.com/v1/notebooks" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN"

```

```
const resp = await fetch("https://notebook.googleapis.com/v1/notebooks", {
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${oauthAccessToken}`,
  },
});

console.log(await resp.json());

```

For details on OAuth 2.0 flows for web servers, installed apps, and client-side applications, see Using OAuth 2.0 to Access Google APIs.

## Quickstart for local development with Application Default Credentials

If you want to try the REST API in your local development environment without creating an OAuth 2.0 client ID first, you can use Application Default Credentials (ADC) with the `gcloud` CLI.

 Generate a local token with the gcloud CLI

Enable the API in your Google Cloud project and sign in with `gcloud auth application-default login`:

```
export PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"

# Enable the Gemini Notebook API in your Google Cloud project
gcloud services enable notebook.googleapis.com --project="$PROJECT_ID"

# Authenticate with Application Default Credentials and the Gemini Notebook API scope
gcloud auth application-default login \
  --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/notebook"

# Print an access token for local testing
export ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

```

### 2. Make a request in your local environment

When calling the API with a token generated by `gcloud auth application-default`, pass two headers in your request:

- `Authorization`: The Bearer token from `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token`.
- `x-goog-user-project`: The ID of your Google Cloud project that has `notebook.googleapis.com` enabled (used as the quota project for the request).

```
curl -s -X GET "https://notebook.googleapis.com/v1/notebooks" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "x-goog-user-project: $PROJECT_ID"

```

```
import os
import requests

headers = {
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['ACCESS_TOKEN']}",
    "x-goog-user-project": os.environ["PROJECT_ID"],
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
}

resp = requests.get("https://notebook.googleapis.com/v1/notebooks", headers=headers)
print(resp.json())

```

auth.title: Authentication - NBLM Docs
highlights:
# Authentication Guide ¶

This guide covers all authentication methods supported by nblm-rs for accessing the NotebookLM Enterprise API.

## Overview ¶

nblm-rs supports three authentication methods:

| Method | Use Case | Operations Support | Recommended |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gcloud CLI | Local development, interactive use | Full (read + write) | ✓ Yes |
| Environment Variable | CI/CD, automation, production | Full (read + write) | For automation |
| OAuth2 (CLI + Python) | End-user scenarios requiring OAuth consent | CLI: Full, Python: Read-only | For NotebookLM users |

## Method 1: gcloud CLI (Recommended) ¶

Uses your Google Cloud user account credentials via the gcloud CLI.

### Prerequisites ¶

```
# Install gcloud CLI
# See: https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install

# Authenticate
gcloud auth login

# Set project (optional)
gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID

```

### CLI Usage ¶

```
# Using gcloud authentication (default)
nblm --project-number PROJECT_NUMBER \
  --location global \
  --endpoint-location global \
  notebooks recent

# Using gcloud authentication
#  (when you specify --auth gcloud, the CLI automatically runs `gcloud auth print-access-token` internally to obtain the access token for authentication)
nblm --auth gcloud \
  --project-number PROJECT_NUMBER \
  --location global \
  --endpoint-location global \
  notebooks recent

```

### Python Usage ¶

```
from nblm import NblmClient, GcloudTokenProvider

# Initialize with gcloud auth
token_provider = GcloudTokenProvider()
client = NblmClient(
    project_number="YOUR_PROJECT_NUMBER",
    location="global",
    endpoint_location="global",
    token_provider=token_provider,
)

# Use the client
notebook = client.create_notebook(title="My Notebook")
print(f"Created: {notebook.name}")

```

...

## Method 2: Environment Variable ¶

Uses an access token from an environment variable. Suitable for CI/CD pipelines.

### Setup ¶

```
# Get access token from your authenticated account
export NBLM_ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)

# Or use any other source of valid access token
export NBLM_ACCESS_TOKEN="ya29...."

```

Token lifetime

Tokens acquired via `gcloud auth print-access-token` — and any environment variables that reuse them — expire after roughly one hour. Refresh them regularly and, for unattended workloads, favor tokens issued from a dedicated service account or Workload Identity Federation with automatic rotation.

...

## Method 3: OAuth2 (User Authentication) ¶

Use this when you need to act as a specific Google user. The CLI completes the OAuth2 browser flow and stores a refresh token in `~/.config/nblm-rs/credentials.json`. Python can then reuse that token in a read-only fashion.

Experimental feature

OAuth2 support is still considered experimental. Set `NBLM_PROFILE_EXPERIMENT=1` before using `--auth user-oauth`, and be prepared for breaking changes while the implementation stabilizes.

### Prerequisites ¶

1. In Google Cloud Console, create an OAuth 2.0 Desktop application client ID for your project.
2. Copy both the client ID and the generated client secret; they must be provided via `NBLM_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` and `NBLM_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`.
3. Ensure the redirect URI `http://127.0.0.1:4317` is allowed (add it if necessary).

### Setup ¶

```
export NBLM_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID="YOUR_CLIENT_ID"
nblm --auth user-oauth --project-number PROJECT_NUMBER notebooks list

```

### Python Usage ¶

```
from nblm import NblmClient

client = NblmClient.with_user_oauth(
    project_number=PROJECT_NUMBER,
    location="global",
)

```

If you need direct access to the provider (for dependency injection or advanced scenarios), instantiate it explicitly:

```
from nblm import UserOAuthProvider

provider = UserOAuthProvider.from_file(project_number=PROJECT_NUMBER)

```

Python scope

The Python SDK currently supports read-only access via OAuth2. All write operations still require the CLI.

gate.title: Rate limits and quotas  |  Gemini Notebook API  |  Google for Developers
highlights:
Rate limits and quotas

The Gemini Notebook API is free to use during the Public Preview period, subject to the following request rate limits and account capacity quotas.

## Request rate limits Copy link to this section: Request rate limits

Rate limits are enforced both per Google Cloud project and per authenticated Google user:

### Per-project rate limits Copy link to this section: Per-project rate limits

| Quota metric | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Read requests (`GetNotebook`, `ListNotebooks`, `GetSource`, `ListSources`) | 100 requests per minute (RPM) per project |
| Write requests (`CreateNotebook`, `UpdateNotebook`, `CreateSource`, `UploadSource`) | 100 requests per minute (RPM) per project |

### Per-user rate limits Copy link to this section: Per-user rate limits

| Method | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| `CreateSource` | 20 requests per minute (RPM) per user |
| `UploadSource` | 20 uploads per minute per user |
| All other methods (`CreateNotebook`, `GetNotebook`, `ListNotebooks`, `UpdateNotebook`, `GetSource`, `ListSources`) | 60 requests per minute (RPM) per user per method |

When a rate limit is exceeded, the API returns HTTP `429 Too Many Requests` (`RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`). Retry failed requests using exponential backoff with jitter. For `UploadSource`, the error includes a `RetryInfo` with the delay before you can start another upload.

## Source size limits

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Maximum source length | 500,000 words per source |
| Maximum inline `text_content` payload size | 1,000,000 bytes (1 MB) |
| Maximum uploaded file size (`UploadSource`) | 200 MiB (209,715,200 bytes) |
| Maximum notebook or source `displayName` length | 500 characters |

## Account tier quotas

Maximum notebook and source counts depend on the authenticated user's subscription tier:

| Tier | Maximum notebooks per user | Maximum sources per notebook |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | 100 | 50 |
| Plus | 200 | 100 |
| Pro | 500 | 300 |
| Ultra | 500 | 600 |

gate.title: Get licenses for NotebookLM Enterprise  |  Google Cloud Documentation
highlights:
## About licenses

To sign in to the NotebookLM Enterprise app, a user must have a license. Licenses can be assigned to users manually or automatically.

- Manually-assigned licenses: These belong to an individual user and are associated with the user's email address.

Manually-assigned licenses are best for users who rely on the NotebookLM Enterprise app and use it often.
- Automatically-assigned licenses: You can choose to have licenses that are part of a subscription be automatically assigned to a user the first time that the user accesses the NotebookLM Enterprise interface. This is a way to distribute licenses in bulk without having to assign licenses to each individual separately.

Licenses are specific to multi-region. For example, if users want access to notebooks in both the `us` multi-region and `global`, assign them a license in each.

## About subscriptions

You buy licenses by the subscription. A subscription contains at least 15 licenses and can contain up to 5,000 licenses. If you need more than 5,000 licenses, contact your Google sales representative.

Subscriptions are specific to multi-regions. Users who create notebooks in the global region need licenses from a `global` subscription. Similarly, users who need to keep their notebooks and data in the European Union need licenses from an `eu` subscription.

There are two subscription tiers for NotebookLM Enterprise:

- The free-trial tier: With this tier, you get a full-featured, 14-day trial subscription of 5000 licenses.
- The paid tier: You can buy a monthly subscription or a year-long subscription. Both the monthly and the yearly subscriptions can be set to renew automatically.

## Before you begin

Before starting the procedures on this page, make sure that:

- You have completed the tasks on the Set up NotebookLM Enterprise. This includes granting at least the `Cloud NotebookLM User` role to any users who you'll license to use NotebookLM Enterprise.
- You have the following roles:

- Cloud NotebookLM Admin
- Gemini Enterprise Admin

## Get a subscription

To get a subscription for NotebookLM Enterprise, do the following:

1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the Gemini Enterprise page.

Gemini Enterprise 
2. Click Manage users.
3. Choose a Multi-region for your subscription. If you don't have compliance or regulatory reasons to locate your data in the US or EU multi-regions, Google recommends that you choose the global region for maximum availability and low latency.
4. Click add Add subscription.
5. On the Add subscription page:

1. Enter the Number of licenses that you want.
2. Choose the Term for the subscription.
3. Optional: Click Auto renew.
4. Select your tier.
6. Click Add.

...

A service endpoint is a base URL that specifies the network address of an API service. One service might have multiple service endpoints. This service has the following service endpoint and all URIs below are relative to this service endpoint:

gcloud auth application-default login \
  --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/notebook"

export ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

```

See Authentication for details on OAuth 2.0 scopes, personal Google Account requirements, and one-time Gemini Notebook sign-in prerequisites.

## Configure an MCP client

Add the remote HTTP MCP server using the `claude mcp add` command:

```
claude mcp add gemini-notebook-api \
  --transport http https://notebook.googleapis.com/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  --header "x-goog-user-project: $PROJECT_ID"

```

Add the server to `.cursor/mcp.json` in your project root (or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` globally):

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gemini-notebook-api": {
      "url": "https://notebook.googleapis.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN",
        "x-goog-user-project": "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
      }
    }
  }
}

```

For any MCP client that supports remote Streamable HTTP servers, configure the endpoint URL and headers:

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gemini-notebook-api": {
      "url": "https://notebook.googleapis.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN",
        "x-goog-user-project": "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
      }
    }
  }
}

```

Note: Access tokens minted using `gcloud auth application-default
print-access-token` expire after one hour. Refresh the token when it expires.

## Available MCP tools

The MCP server exposes 7 tools corresponding to the REST API methods:

| Tool name | Description | Required arguments | Optional arguments |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `create_notebook` | Creates a new notebook. | `notebook` (`{"displayName": "..."}`) | — |
| `get_notebook` | Gets metadata for a notebook. | `name` (`notebooks/{notebook}`) | — |
| `list_notebooks` | Lists notebooks accessible to the caller. | — | `pageSize`, `pageToken`, `filter` (`notebook.is_owner = true` or `notebook.is_owner = false`) |
| `update_notebook` | Updates a notebook's display name. | `notebook` (`{"name": "notebooks/{notebook}", "displayName": "..."}`) | `updateMask` (`displayName`) |
| `create_source` | Ingests a web URL, YouTube video, plain text, or Markdown source into a notebook. | `parent` (`notebooks/{notebook}`), `source` (`{"displayName": "...", "webContent": {"url": "..."}}` or `{"displayName": "...", "mimeType": "text/markdown", "textContent": {"content": "..."}}`) | — |
| `get_source` | Gets metadata and processing state (`PROCESSING`, `ACTIVE`, `FAILED`) for a source. | `name` (`notebooks/{notebook}/sources/{source}`) | — |
| `list_sources` | Lists all sources in a notebook. | `parent` (`notebooks/{notebook}`) | `pageSize`, `pageToken` |

Note: File uploads aren't available as an MCP tool. To upload a file, call the REST `UploadSource` endpoint.

highlights:
# MCP server guide

**Last Updated:** 2026-11-06

> **Experimental / preview.** The MCP server ships behind the optional `mcp` extra. Its
> tool surface (names, parameters, output shapes) is **not** covered by the library's semver
> guarantees and may change between releases. `pip install notebooklm-py` is unaffected — the
> server and its dependencies only arrive with the `mcp` extra.

The MCP server exposes NotebookLM to any Model Context Protocol
client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, …) as a set of **39 tools** — manage
notebooks and sources, chat over a notebook's sources, generate and download studio artifacts,
and run deep research. It is a thin adapter over the same business logic the CLI uses, so it
behaves identically to `notebooklm <command>`.

See the MCP subsystem diagram for process and
application boundaries. Remote file movement is expanded in the
transfer-security data flow.
The operator-facing hosting threat model is SECURITY.md.

## Install

The server is behind the `mcp` extra (pulls in `fastmcp`):

```bash
pip install "notebooklm-py[mcp]"
# or run with no install, straight from PyPI:
uvx --from "notebooklm-py[mcp]" notebooklm-mcp --help
```

## Authenticate (once)

The server reuses a stored profile — it does **not** log in on its own. For the
default Web backend, authenticate once before starting it:

```bash
notebooklm login
# or, if you didn't install the package:
uvx --from "notebooklm-py[mcp]" notebooklm login
```

Credentials are stored per profile under `~/.notebooklm/`. The server binds the **active profile**
at startup (override with `--profile`, below). See configuration.md for profiles
and multi-account setup.

For `--backend android`, include Android plus the browser needed for the one-time
interactive bootstrap, then initialize the same profile the server will bind:

```bash
pip install "notebooklm-py[mcp,android,browser]"
notebooklm --profile work login --master-token --account you@example.com
notebooklm-mcp --profile work --backend android
```

After bootstrap, the MCP runtime needs `[mcp,android]`; `[browser]` can be
omitted from a separate deployment environment. You can also bootstrap without
Playwright by supplying the one-time `--oauth-token` documented in the
installation guide.
Android mints bearer credentials from that durable profile token when the
server opens; a cookie-only profile and `NOTEBOOKLM_AUTH_JSON` are Web-only
authentication inputs.

## Connect a client

The fastest path is the auto-config command, which writes the server block into a client's MCP
config (idempotent, never clobbers other servers):

```bash
notebooklm mcp install claude-desktop   # or: claude-code | cursor | windsurf
```

| Client | Config written |
|--------|----------------|
| `claude-desktop` | `claude_desktop_config.json` (per-OS location) |
| `claude-code` | `~/.claude.json` (user scope) |
| `cursor` | `~/.cursor/mcp.json` |
| `windsurf` | `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json` |

It writes a block that launches the server via `uvx` (so only `uv` needs to be on the host):

```jsonc
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "notebooklm": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["--from", "notebooklm-py[mcp]", "notebooklm-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Restart the client after installing. For a one-click Claude Desktop bundle,
download `notebooklm-mcp.mcpb` from the
latest release
(**Assets**) and use "Install Extension"; see
`desktop-extension/README.md` for details.

## Run it directly

The console script is `notebooklm-mcp`:

```bash
notebooklm-mcp                         # stdio transport (default — for desktop hosts)
notebooklm-mcp --profile work          # bind a specific auth profile
notebooklm-mcp --read-only             # register only read-only tools (omit mutating/destructive tools)
notebooklm-mcp --backend android        # Android adapters; requires Android auth setup
notebooklm-mcp --transport http        # loopback streamable-HTTP on 127.0.0.1:9420
notebooklm-mcp --transport http --port 9000
```

| Flag | Default | Notes |
|------|---------|-------|
| `--profile` | active profile | which stored auth profile the process binds |
| `--read-only` | `false` | register only `readOnlyHint` tools (`NOTEBOOKLM_MCP_READ_ONLY=1`); mutating/destructive tools and file-transfer routes are omitted |
| `--backend` | `web` | `web` or `android`; overrides `NOTEBOOKLM_BACKEND` |
| `--transport` | `stdio` | `stdio` (subprocess hosts) or `http` (loopback) |
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | http only; non-loopback is **refused** unless `NOTEBOOKLM_MCP_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_BIND=1` |
| `--port` | `9420` | http only |
| `--log-level` | `INFO` | logs go to **stderr**; stdout stays pure JSON-RPC |

There is no `--token` flag — the HTTP bearer token is **env-only**
(`NOTEBOOKLM_MCP_TOKEN`) so it cannot leak via `ps aux`.

`stdio` is right for Claude Desktop/Code, Cursor, and Windsurf (they launch the server as a
subprocess). Use `http` for a local web client or to share one running server across clients on
the same machine. The HTTP transport is loopback-only by default; binding to a non-loopback
address requires **both** the explicit `NOTEBOOKLM_MCP_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_BIND=1` override **and**
auth (`NOTEBOOKLM_MCP_TOKEN` and/or OAuth) — the server fails closed (refuses to start) on a
network bind without auth, since it fronts a full Google account.

**Loopback HTTP may be tokenless.** A default `127.0.0.1` bind does not require
`NOTEBOOKLM_MCP_TOKEN`. The Host-header DNS-rebinding guard still rejects requests whose
`Host` is not a loopback literal. See SECURITY.md.

mcp.title: sanjeev7e/notebooklm-mcp
highlights:
# notebooklm-mcp-rpc

A pure-TypeScript Model Context Protocol server for Google NotebookLM. Speaks Google's undocumented `batchexecute` RPC protocol directly — no Python runtime, no `notebooklm` CLI, no shelling out. Deploys cleanly to Vercel Node functions.

> Companion / sibling project to `notebooklm-mcp`, which wraps the `notebooklm-py` CLI as a subprocess. Pick this one if you want zero Python dependencies and seamless serverless deployment.

## What's in the box

- **Native RPC client** — encoder/decoder for the `batchexecute` wire format ported faithfully from `notebooklm-py`'s `_core.py` and `rpc/`.
- **Native chat client** — POSTs to the streaming `GenerateFreeFormStreamed` endpoint and parses the chunked response.
- **51 MCP tools** spanning notebooks, sources, chat, artifacts (all 9 generation types + downloads), notes, research, sharing, and language settings.
- **Auth refresh** — concurrent-safe re-scrape of `SNlM0e` / `FdrFJe` on 401/403.
- **Stdio + Streamable-HTTP** transports. Vercel adapter included.
- **Strict TypeScript**: `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, full Zod input validation.

...

## Authentication

You need a valid Google session. The simplest path is to bootstrap it once with the Python `notebooklm` CLI, then point this server at the resulting file:

```bash
pip install "notebooklm-py[browser]"
playwright install chromium
notebooklm login        # writes ~/.notebooklm/storage_state.json
```

Now choose one of:

| Variable | Use when |
|---|---|
| `NOTEBOOKLM_STORAGE_PATH` | Local dev. Path to `storage_state.json`. |
| `NOTEBOOKLM_AUTH_JSON` | Serverless / CI. Inline JSON contents of the same file. |
| `NOTEBOOKLM_COOKIES` + `NOTEBOOKLM_CSRF_TOKEN` + `NOTEBOOKLM_SESSION_ID` | You already have tokens from another pipeline. |

Cookies do expire. When they do, `auth_status` will return an `isError: true` result with `reason: "auth"` and a reminder to re-run the login step.

## Tool catalog (51)

| Group | Tools |
|---|---|
| Auth / status | `auth_status` |
| Notebooks | `notebook_list`, `notebook_create`, `notebook_rename`, `notebook_delete`, `notebook_raw` |
| Sources | `source_list`, `source_add_url`, `source_add_text`, `source_delete`, `source_rename`, `source_refresh`, `source_fulltext`, `source_guide`, `source_wait` |
| Chat | `chat_ask`, `chat_history`, `chat_last_conversation_id`, `chat_configure` |
| Artifacts | `artifact_list`, `artifact_get`, `artifact_delete`, `artifact_rename`, `artifact_wait` |
| Generation | `generate_audio`, `generate_video`, `generate_cinematic_video`, `generate_report`, `generate_quiz`, `generate_flashcards`, `generate_infographic`, `generate_slide_deck`, `generate_data_table`, `generate_mind_map`, `revise_slide` |
| Downloads | `download_artifact` (one tool, dispatches by artifact type — writes to `outputPath` or returns inline base64/text) |
| Notes | `note_list`, `note_create`, `note_update`, `note_delete` |
| Research | `research_start`, `research_poll`, `research_wait`, `research_import_all` |
| Sharing | `share_status`, `share_set_public`, `share_set_view_level`, `share_add_user`, `share_remove_user` |
| Language | `language_get`, `language_set` |

...

- **No file uploads**.

...

|---|---|---|
| Python runtime needed | Yes (CLI subprocess) | No |
| Vercel-deployable | Only with custom container | Plain Node function |

...

| Setup steps | install Python + CLI + login | login once, then JS-only |

mcp.title: moodRobotics/notebooklm-mcp-server
highlights:
## 💡 What is this?

Google's **Gemini Notebook** (renamed from NotebookLM in July 2026) is the best grounded-answer engine on the market: it only answers from the sources you give it, with citations. This MCP server hands that power to your AI agents — Claude, Gemini, Antigravity, Cursor and any other MCP client — so they can build notebooks, run Deep Research, generate podcasts, videos, quizzes, flashcards, reports and mind maps, take notes, and share the results with your team. **All programmatically, with zero hallucinations.**

> [!NOTE]
> **NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook.** Google renamed the product on July 16, 2026 (see notebook.google). Same product, same notebooks, same API surface — this server keeps working unchanged, and the npm package keeps its `notebooklm-mcp-server` name.

## 🚀 Installation

### Option 1 — Global install (recommended)

```bash
npm install -g notebooklm-mcp-server
```

> [!NOTE]
> The server checks for updates on startup and keeps itself current automatically.

### Option 2 — Zero-install with NPX

```bash
npx -y notebooklm-mcp-server auth   # authenticate
npx -y notebooklm-mcp-server start  # run the server
```

## 🔑 Authentication

1. Run the interactive login (opens a Chromium window):

```bash
npx notebooklm-mcp-server auth
```

2. Sign in with your Google account. When the notebook list appears, the session cookies (including Google's rotating `__Secure-1PSIDTS` token) are captured and saved to `~/.notebooklm-mcp/auth.json`.

3. Done — the server loads the session automatically and refreshes the rotating token by itself.

> [!TIP]
> If the session ever expires, run `npx notebooklm-mcp-server auth` again in a terminal, then call the `refresh_auth` MCP tool (or just restart your client) to pick up the new cookies without reconfiguring anything.

...

## 📖 Tool Reference

47 tools, grouped by what they do. Full parameter signatures live in docs/TOOLS.md.

### 📒 Notebooks

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `notebook_list` | List all notebooks with sources and metadata |
| `notebook_create` | Create a new notebook |
| `notebook_get` | Get one notebook's details and source IDs |
| `notebook_rename` | Rename a notebook |
| `notebook_delete` | Delete a notebook (requires `confirm`) |
| `notebook_summarize` | AI notebook guide: summary + suggested questions |
| `prompts_suggest` | AI-suggested prompts to ask about the sources |

### 🔗 Sharing

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `notebook_share` | Toggle public link and/or manage collaborators by email |
| `notebook_share_status` | Read the current sharing configuration |

### 🖇️ Sources

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `notebook_add_url` | Add a website or YouTube video as a source |
| `notebook_add_text` | Add pasted text as a source |
| `notebook_add_drive` | Add a Google Drive document as a source |
| `notebook_add_local_file` | Upload a local PDF / TXT / Markdown file |
| `source_get_guide` | AI guide for one source: summary + key topics |
| `source_rename` | Rename a source |
| `source_check_freshness` | Check if a URL/Drive source has newer content |
| `source_sync` | Re-sync a Drive source to the latest content |
| `source_delete` | Delete a source (requires `confirm`) |

...

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is an unofficial community project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google. It relies on reverse-engineered internal APIs that may change without notice; use it with a Google account you are comfortable automating.
